form: Open grassy river bank under mature shade trees, sloping down to a still reed-edged backwater of the upper Thames; no built structure in the playing area
period: Friday 4 July 1862, Thames valley near Oxford; unimproved water-meadow bank of the clergyman-scholar family's afternoon walk

structure.item: grassy bank about 1.2 m high, sloping at roughly 25 degrees from level meadow down to the waterline, with a flat shelf under the trees where the sister sits
reed-edged backwater with still water beside the bank on the water side of the plan (the 'neighbouring pool')
the open field runs off level behind the bank toward the hawthorn hedge (links to SCN-field-hedge-burrow)
background only: the roofline and tall chimneys of the family's gabled polychrome-brick villa above the far hedge, about 400 m away, so 'run in to your tea' has a visible goal
structure.why: The house is 'a short run away' (ch012-p66); an 1860s north-Oxford Gothic Revival villa fits a senior clergyman-scholar household and is the waking root of the White Rabbit's house

structure.item: background only: a slender stone parish-church spire on the far skyline, never approached
structure.why: Bible registers the spire as a wide-shot landmark only

materials.item: close meadow turf with daisies and buttercups
bare trodden earth and exposed tree roots at the lip of the bank
materials.why: Real river-bank erosion gives the sister's seat a physical edge

materials.item: reed beds of common reed and reedmace standing 1.5 to 2 m tall at the backwater edge
still, dark-green river water with a slight surface ripple

details.item: two or three mature English elms and a pollarded crack willow overhanging the bank, the elm sheds a few early dead leaves onto the grass (waking root of the flying pack of cards)
details.note: tree species inferred from Thames-valley hedgerow country, culture_ref geography.json#LOC-riverside-region.physical.flora

details.item: daisies thick enough on the bank to make a daisy-chain
yellow flag irises and water-lily pads in the shallows of the backwater
details.why: Native midsummer Thames backwater plants; gives the reeds a readable foreground

scale_notes.rule: Waking frame is always true scale (1:1). Alice = 135 cm (CHAR-alice appearance anchor); this set is the reference against which every dream scale build is measured. No forced perspective or scaled set here (SUP-003 applies inside the dream only).

negative: no stone or concrete embankment, no revetment, no steps down to the water
no towpath fencing, no wire fences, no park benches, no signposts
no boats with engines, no moorings or jetties in frame
no bridges, lock gates or weirs in frame
no telegraph poles, pylons or later buildings on the skyline
no tended lawn or flower borders; this is a rough water-meadow
no tropical or ornamental trees (no palms, no weeping cherry)
no autumn-coloured canopy; the trees are full green midsummer foliage with only a few fallen dead leaves
prompt_ready_en: a grassy midsummer riverbank near Oxford in 1862, sloping to a still reed-edged backwater, shaded by mature elms and a pollarded willow, daisies and buttercups in close meadow turf, a few dead leaves on the grass, a distant stone church spire and the gabled brick roofline of a Victorian villa beyond a far hedge
